title: Runtime triage + handoff: emergency batching fixes and cache eviction observations
content:
Summary

Quick sync from the emergency triage session (Mon 2026-05-11 09:00 PT) and handoff notes for on-call. We uncovered two separate but interacting regressions after the micro-batching kernel patch rolled on Friday night: 1) a change in the kernel kernel-selection fallback logic causing suboptimal matmul kernels at sequence lengths > 1k, and 2) an aggressive KV-cache eviction heuristic that triggers when GPU memory pressure crosses a lower-than-intended threshold. The combination increased p95 token latency for some chat traffic spikes by ~45% and increased GPU memory churn which in turn amplified GC-like stalls.

Attendees
- Priya Raman (triage lead)
- Ethan Morales (kernel lead)
- Sofia Nguyen (SRE / observability)
- Hugo Alvarez (batching experiments)
- Lina Chen (on-call)
- Daniel Park (release engineering, remote)

What we observed (raw notes)
- Incident window: 2026-05-10 23:40 PT -> 2026-05-11 03:20 PT
- P95 token latency spike: baseline 210ms -> 305ms in worst buckets for hosted-api/chat route (model: rw-large-1.1b-quant)
- GPU mem orphaning: saw repeated peaks at ~94% then immediate evictions; previously steady at ~88%
- Batch sizes dropped unexpectedly during spikes (mean batch size for 1s windows: 8 -> 3) leading to throughput loss
- Trace IDs: trace-20260511-09:12:44: see linked APM traces in Slack thread

Root cause hypothesis (current)
1) Kernel fallback ordering change (PR 3421) introduced earlier selection of a conservative matmul kernel for sequences > 1024 when quantized kernels are present. That kernel has worse latency at small batch sizes; when traffic variably drops batch sizes due to KV evictions, p95 rises.
2) KV-cache eviction threshold was tightened in a config tweak (infra config commit: release/dev-config#558) that reduces memory headroom from 12% to 6% before eviction — that makes minor memory spikes trigger aggressive prefix cache eviction which increases recompute for cold requests.
3) Interaction effect: smaller batches + recompute = more kernel invocations on a kernel that scales poorly for those shapes.

Evidence we collected
- Flamegraphs attached in PR comment (see PR 3421) show increased kernel dispatch count for attention matmul at timestamps matching latency spikes.
- Heap snapshots (gpu-mem-snap-20260511-00z) show sudden decrease in cached KV tables concurrent with increased host-side scheduling latency.
- A/B micro-experiment (see results below) where we reverted kernel fallback order on 3 nodes showed p95 drop back to 220ms within 12 minutes.

Immediate mitigation applied (May 11 01:30 PT)
- Rolled back the kernel fallback change to the previous selection order on the small canary fleet (canary-nodes-08/09/10).
- Tuned KV-cache eviction threshold back to 12% headroom in release/dev-config#559 and pushed to Dedicated staging.
- Enabled a temporary aggressive batching attempt: allow micro-batcher to wait up to 40ms (was 20ms) when avg batch size < 4 during sustained spikes (experiment flag: runtime.experiments.wait_longer_low_batch).

Short experiment log (May 11 02:00–03:00 PT)
- Variant A (rollback fallback) on 3 nodes: p50 85ms -> 88ms, p95 220ms -> 225ms (stable)
- Variant B (keep fallback + kv-threshold revert) on 3 nodes: p95 260ms -> 235ms after threshold revert
- Variant C (fallback + threshold revert + wait_longer flag) on 2 nodes: p95 215ms -> 210ms and batch size recovered to mean 7.6
- Conclusion: combination of threshold revert + longer micro-batcher wait produced best short term recovery.

Open issues / longer-term follow-ups
- Kernel selection policy: the current policy lacks a signal for runtime batch-size distribution. We should add a small heuristic to prefer kernels that perform better at the observed runtime batch-size/seq-len histogram (RFC: kernel-selection-adaptive-2026-05). Owner: Ethan. ETA: EOD 2026-05-18 for first draft.
- KV cache eviction policy: need a more workload-aware eviction that considers request QPS variance and model prefix hit rate rather than only memory headroom. Suggestion: track per-model prefix reuse rate (in telemetry) and base eviction on TTL *and* reuse score. Owner: Hugo. ETA: 2026-05-25 for POC.
- Batching policy knobs: the ad-hoc wait_longer flag helped but we need a principled adaptive micro-batcher that increases wait when batch size is low and latency SLOs allow it. Owner: Lina + Hugo. Spike: 2w.
- Regression test: add an e2e perf test that replays mixed sequence-length chat traffic to catch kernel fallback regressions. Add to CI perf-suite. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-06-01.

Action items (owners and due dates)
- Ethan: Draft kernel-selection-adaptive RFC, include simple opt-in heuristic based on recent observed batch-size histogram. Due 2026-05-18.
- Hugo: Implement telemetry metric for prefix reuse and create POC eviction algorithm. Due 2026-05-25.
- Lina: Convert emergency fixes into a staged rollback playbook for on-call (how to revert fallback and change kv threshold safely). Due 2026-05-14.
- Priya: Add a regression test case to perf-suite that simulates mid-load batch collapse and validates p95 thresholds. Due 2026-06-01.
- Daniel: Coordinate a quick release to staging with config revert and wait_longer flag enabled for further 24h observation. Due 2026-05-12.

Notes to self / rough checklist
- Attach links to the heap snapshots and APM traces (TODO before closing doc).
- Postmortem draft if sla breach confirmed: assign after final numbers in 48h.
- Keep canary nodes under tighter monitoring for next 36h (SRE: Sofia).

Handoff for on-call (Lina)
- Current status: mitigations in place on staging and partial canaries. Runbook: if p95 > 400ms for > 15m on hosted-api/chat, perform the staged rollback (playbook steps 1..6).
- Temporary feature flags to toggle: runtime.feature.kernel_pref_fallback_v2, runtime.config.kv_headroom_pct, runtime.experiments.wait_longer_low_batch.
- Key traces to check: trace-20260511-09:12:44, trace-20260511-02:04:17.
- Contact points: Ethan (kernels), Hugo (batching), Priya (triage).

Misc brainstorm items (freeform)
- Could we use a tiny ML classifier to predict if a request will be prefix-cache-heavy and pre-warm relevant KV entries during queueing? (nice but probably overkill).
- Explore lightweight per-tenant eviction budgets so noisy tenants don't thrash global KV.
- Consider adding a cross-check in kernel selector: "if avg_batch_size_last_30s < 6 choose small-batch-optimized kernel". Quick win.

Appendix / artifacts to attach (TODO)

- Heap snapshots (gpu-mem-snap-20260511-00z)
- PR 3421 diff and benchmark spreadsheet (benchmarks/rw-large-kernel-comparison-2026-05-10.csv)

End of notes.

(Informal, rough — will iterate into a short postmortem if SLA impact confirmed)
